Question: Yan is somewhere between his home and the stadium. To get to the stadium he can walk directly to the stadium, or else he can walk home and then ride his bicycle to the stadium. He rides \(7\) times as fast as he walks, and both choices require the same amount of time. What is the ratio of Yan’s distance from his home to his distance from the stadium?
Solution:
Divide the entire home-to-stadium distance into seven equal parts. Since Yan rides seven times as fast as he walks, riding all seven parts takes the same time as walking one part.

Thus walking home and then cycling to the stadium takes the walking time for his distance home plus one extra part. For this to equal the time spent walking directly to the stadium, his distance to the stadium must be one part longer than his distance home.

These two distances add to seven parts. Removing the extra part leaves six parts split equally, so his distance home is \(6\div2=3\) parts and his distance to the stadium is \(4\) parts. The requested ratio is therefore \(\dfrac34\), choice B.
